concerns.text: Task T020 implements a 'Spatial Split' (Eastern/Western US) and T028-T029 implement 'Linear Mixed-Effects Model (LMM)' and 'paired t-test'. This directly violates Spec FR-004 (mandates 'temporal split'), Spec FR-006 (mandates 'Diebold-Mariano test'), and Constitution Principle VII (mandates 'temporal split'). The tasks silently replace the required scientific methodology with an unauthorized alternative.

Task T032 generates 'continental-scale maps' for the 'Continental US'. This violates Spec FR-007 (requires continental maps) but contradicts the Plan.md which explicitly reduced scope to 'Lake Powell region' due to data constraints. The task fails to align with the Plan's scope reduction, creating a deliverable that cannot be executed with the verified data, effectively weakening the feasibility constraint.

Task T030 flags findings if 'mean absolute difference > 3 days'. Spec SC-003 and US-3 Acceptance Scenario 3 explicitly require flagging if variation 'exceeds 7 days'. This is a silent relaxation of the acceptance criteria, weakening the robustness requirement.

Task T036 sets a RAM threshold of '> 5GB' to trigger refactoring. Spec SC-004 explicitly defines the constraint as '≤ 7 GB RAM'. This silently relaxes the performance constraint, allowing the pipeline to run with up to 7GB of memory without triggering the required optimization, violating the feasibility requirement.

Task T004 configures 'EASTERN_US_BOUNDS' and 'WESTERN_US_BOUNDS'. This contradicts the Plan.md which explicitly reduced the scope to 'Lake Powell region' and states 'All maps and predictions are confined to this region'. The task introduces configuration for a scope (Continental US split) that the Plan has explicitly discarded, violating the scope constraint.
